text: This run belongs to the Sun, held within the long Mars period. Mars keeps the pitch of the years, the effort and the contest, while the Sun decides what the effort is about. Usually it is about you. Work that carries your name tends to demand pushing now, and the fights that matter are the ones where standing down would cost you something you care about being. Ambition sharpens. You may compete openly rather than quietly, or take a role that puts you in front of people who will judge how you handle pressure. Dealings with authority can heat up in this stretch, whether that means a boss, a mentor, or your own reluctance to defer. Pride is the thing to watch. When effort and identity fuse, an ordinary disagreement starts to feel like a verdict on your worth, and that is how a small conflict grows expensive. The same fusion is what makes the run productive, since courage comes easier when the cause is plainly yours. Vitality generally runs high, sometimes past what your body wants to spend, and this stretch repays exertion aimed at one clear thing rather than scattered across several. You take from it a sharper sense of what you are willing to be seen fighting for.

Venus takes its turn as sub-lord partway through the Mars chapter, and the temperature changes without dropping. The larger years remain the ones of drive and contest; Venus works inside them by giving the drive a subject, which is people, pleasure, and what you actually want. Desire gets more definite in this run. Attractions arrive with force behind them, and relationships already in motion often speed up, for better and for worse. Some of the sharpest exchanges in the whole chapter happen with people you love, because closeness gives the heat somewhere to go. That is a description rather than a warning. A stretch like this tends to surface the argument a partnership has been postponing, and dealt with directly it clears the air, while charm alone only defers the bill. Making things goes well here too. Craft that takes physical effort, anything you build or shape with your hands, gets the energy and the eye it needs at the same time. Money and taste can turn contentious, since Mars spends and Venus wants, and the pair can run through resources faster than you notice. The gift of the run is that force learns to negotiate. You get practice at saying plainly what you want while staying in relation to the person across from you, and the rest of the chapter keeps asking for that skill.

When Mercury comes up as sub-lord inside the Mars period, the fight moves into words. Firdaria nests its periods, a shorter run under a long one, so the chapter's push carries on while Mercury handles the tactics. Argument is the signature of this stretch. Debates, negotiations, disputes over terms, correspondence with an edge to it, all of these tend to multiply, and you are rarely the passive party. Your speech gets faster and more pointed, useful when a situation needs precision and costly when a joke lands as a cut. Contracts, paperwork, and the fine print of commitments often ask for attention now, and pushing them through is possible, though haste is the standing hazard. Decisions made at speed here have a way of needing revision later. Study can go unusually well, especially anything with a competitive frame or a deadline: a certification, a case to build, a skill you took up because someone said you could not. Travel tends to be short, frequent, and driven by errands rather than rest. Mentally the run is restless, and sleep can thin out when your mind keeps rehearsing conversations you have not had yet. What the stretch teaches, if you let it, is strategy, which is the difference between winning an exchange and getting what you came for.

The Moon's turn as sub-lord brings the Mars chapter home. While the Moon holds this stretch, the chapter's heat runs through domestic life, the body, and feelings you are used to keeping at a manageable temperature. Household matters get busy. Moves, repairs, changes in who lives with you, care that a family member suddenly needs, this run tends to fill with that kind of activity, and it rarely arrives at a convenient moment. Friction at home is common enough to name plainly. Old family patterns can flare, and irritability lands nearest the people you share a kitchen with. Saying the thing early, while it is still small, is what keeps the run workable. Your moods carry more force than usual and they move quickly, so a feeling can go from nothing to urgent within an afternoon. Energy rises and falls on its own schedule rather than yours, which makes this a stretch where working with your own rhythm gets more done than working against it. Appetite, sleep, and physical restlessness all tend to speak up. The run grows a truer relationship between what you feel and what you do about it. Anger stops being an interruption to daily life and becomes information about it.

Saturn's stretch inside the Mars period is the one where push meets wall. The tradition counts both bodies as hard going, and the pairing sets the chapter's forward drive against the planet whose business is limit, delay, and the real cost of things. Progress slows without stopping. Effort meets more resistance than it did a season ago: approvals that take longer, work that has to be redone, obstacles that are nobody's fault and still stand there. The temptation is to force harder, and force applied to a wall mostly makes heat. Frustration is the honest word for how this can feel, and it helps to know the resistance is the run's material rather than a sign you chose wrong. Used well, the stretch builds. Effort spent on slow structural work, the kind whose payoff sits years out, tends to hold in a way quicker wins do not. Discipline comes more easily than enthusiasm here. Watch what you do with anger you cannot spend, since a run like this can turn it inward as fatigue or park it as a grudge that outlasts its cause. Rest counts as work now. The stretch leaves you with stamina of the unromantic sort, and a clearer view of which of your ambitions were solid enough to survive being slowed down.

Jupiter's run as sub-lord widens the Mars chapter. The long period keeps its appetite for effort, and Jupiter, taking its turn within, adds scope, so what you push for gets bigger and the pushing meets less obstruction than usual. Campaigns started in this stretch tend to find more backing than they would in a cooler season. Someone with standing may take your side, a door you have been leaning on may give, or an opening turns up that rewards exactly the boldness the chapter has been training in you. Ambition feels justified now, and often is. Travel, legal matters, teaching, and dealings with large institutions can all become active, usually with some heat in them. Confidence is both the resource and the risk. This pairing is generous with yes, and a yes given in high spirits can commit years of your life to something you would have thought twice about on a quieter day. Fighting on too many fronts is the classic way to waste the run. Enthusiasm can also outrun your stamina, since energy this good invites you to spend it as though it will not run out. The stretch works best with one main object in view. Taken that way it is among the more rewarding parts of the chapter, a run in which courage is answered rather than merely tested.

Mars begins by holding both offices at once. In firdaria the opening run of a period belongs to the lord of the period itself, so the Mars years start with their subject stated flat, and this is where the chapter shows what it intends to be about. The tradition reads this opening as one of the hotter stretches in the sequence, and demanding is a better word for it than dramatic. Energy tends to arrive before you have decided where to put it, patience can run shorter than usual, and situations you had been handling carefully often reach the point where they have to be handled directly. Things that were merely annoying start to feel intolerable, which is uncomfortable and also how the chapter gets going. Initiative is easy now, and starting is what this run is for: the application sent, the project begun, the conversation opened, the training taken up. Follow-through is a later problem. What you set in motion here often sets the direction the whole seven years take, so early choices matter more than their size suggests. The tradition's standing cautions belong here, and they describe tendencies rather than events: haste makes small mishaps likelier, and words said hot are harder to take back than in a milder run. None of that is a forecast. It is the shape of the pressure, and pressure can be worked with. Physical exertion helps, because the stretch hands you more drive than any single project can absorb. Learning early how you carry your own anger tends to make the rest of the chapter go considerably better.
